Subject: Unexpected charges — duplicate session counts?

Hi Rishi / Monica,

We noticed a sharp spike in our usage charges for Nov 24–26 that doesn't match our activity. The billing line items show repeated token counts tied to the same conversation/session IDs multiple times. Example IDs from our side: conv_8a3f, conv_8a3f:part2, conv_9b12. The top-line overage is ~$147.80 on the invoice posted Nov 27. I attached a screenshot of the billing portal view.

Can you provide a per-session breakdown and confirm whether these were unique requests or double-counted by your metering? We can share raw session logs if that helps. Also, we're EU-based for VAT handling — if this is an error, how will the adjustment appear on the invoice and VAT lines?

Appreciate quick help — this is a live invoice hold for our finance team.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Unexpected charges — duplicate session counts? (export attached)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the sample IDs and the screenshot. I pulled the attribution export and included a trimmed CSV with per-session records: session_counts_20261127.csv (attached). Quick summary:

- Total billed tokens (Nov 24–26): 1,142,890
- Unique session tokens after deduping by request-id + conversation-hash: 1,130,420
- Duplicate-attributed tokens identified: 12,470 (1.09% of the period total)

Root cause (short): we observed several long-lived conversational sessions where the client re-established the socket and re-sent the last chunk without the server-side idempotency header set; our metering pipeline attributed the reconnect as a new session for token attribution in a small subset of cases. We have a mitigation change queued to enforce idempotency headers and drop duplicated deltas during ingestion (PR and rollout planned by 2026-12-02).

Proposed remediation:
- Issue an invoice credit for the duplicated 12,470 tokens (calculated credit = $147.80).
- Reverse VAT on that line item (you listed EU billing).
- Provide a corrected invoice PDF and a note that will appear as a proforma adjustment for Nov.

Attachments: session_counts_20261127.csv (sample rows, columns: conversation_id, request_id, timestamp, billed_tokens, deduped_tokens) and billing_export_2026-11-27.json (billing line items).

If you authorize the credit, we'll submit the adjustment and generate the corrected invoice. If you prefer, we can also issue a one-time invoice-level credit and mark it on your December statement.

/Monica
Monica Patel
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
